subtopicTitle: Centre of mass — derivation for common shapes (rod, triangle, semicircle, hemisphere)

cards.front: State the centre of mass location for a uniform rod of length L lying along the x-axis from 0 to L.
cards.back: At x = L/2 from either end (by symmetry).

cards.front: Derive the x-coordinate of the centre of mass for a uniform rod of length L and mass M along [0,L].
cards.back: $$x_{cm} = \frac{1}{M} \int_0^L x \, dm$$ with dm = (M/L) dx gives $$x_{cm} = \frac{L}{2}$$.

cards.front: State the centre of mass location for a uniform triangular lamina of base B and height H (vertex at origin).
Derive the y-coordinate of the CM for a uniform triangular lamina of height H (base parallel to x-axis).
cards.back: Using similar triangles, width at height y is proportional to (H-y). Integrate $$y_{cm} = \frac{\int_0^H y \cdot (H-y) dy}{\int_0^H (H-y) dy} = H/3$$.

cards.front: Derive the y-coordinate of the centre of mass for a uniform semicircular lamina of radius R.
cards.back: $$y_{cm} = \frac{2R}{\pi}$$ (above the diameter). Use polar coordinates: $$y_{cm} = \frac{\int_0^\pi (R\sin\theta) R d\theta}{\int_0^\pi R d\theta}$$.

cards.front: Derive the z-coordinate of the centre of mass for a solid hemisphere of radius R (flat face on xy-plane).
cards.back: $$z_{cm} = \frac{3R}{8}$$. Volume element in spherical coords yields $$z_{cm} = \frac{3}{8}R$$ after integrating density over the hemisphere.

cards.front: What is the CM distance from the centre for a thin hemispherical shell of radius R?
cards.back: R/2 along the axis of symmetry.
